questions.question: What is the term used to describe the random motion of particles suspended in a medium?
options: Diffusion
Brownian motion
Convection
Osmosis

questions.question: How do suspensions differ from solutions?
options: Suspensions contain visible solid particles that will eventually settle over time
Suspensions are always perfectly clear and never settle
Suspensions are formed only when gases dissolve in liquids
Suspensions cannot be separated by physical means

questions.question: What must happen to the forces of attraction between solute particles for dissolving to occur?
options: They must be strengthened
They must be overcome
They must remain unchanged
They must be completely destroyed and turned into energy

questions.question: When two different liquids are mixed, why might the total volume be less than expected?
options: Some particles evaporate instantly
One type of particle may fit into the spaces between another type
The particles shrink in size upon contact
Mass is lost during the mixing process

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding dissolving and melting?
options: They are the exact same chemical process
Dissolving is a chemical change, while melting is a physical change
Both are physical processes, but dissolving is not the same as melting
Melting requires a solvent, whereas dissolving only requires heat

questions.question: Why is it important to write scientific methods clearly so they are repeatable and reproducible?
options: To ensure other scientists can carry out the investigation and verify the findings
To guarantee that the experiment is only ever performed once
To make sure the experiment requires expensive equipment
To ensure that no variables are kept constant

questions.question: What is formed when a soluble solid successfully dissolves in an appropriate solvent?
options: A suspension
A pure material
A solution
A precipitate

questions.question: If you mix 15 grams of sugar into 150 grams of water, what will be the total mass of the mixture?
options: More than 165 g

questions.question: Which apparatus and unit are correctly matched for measuring volume in a school chemistry laboratory?
options: A balance, measured in grams
A thermometer, measured in degrees Celsius
A measuring cylinder, measured in cm³
A beaker, measured in grams

questions.question: What is a characteristic property of a pure material?
options: It melts and boils over a wide range of temperatures
It has a fixed melting point and boiling point
It consists of multiple types of substances mixed together
Its physical state cannot be changed by heating

questions.question: What effect do impurities have on the melting and boiling points of a material?
options: They have absolutely no effect on either point
They keep the melting and boiling points completely fixed
They change the melting and boiling point of the material
They ensure the material melts and boils at the exact same temperature

questions.question: What can happen to solutes in a solution as the solution is cooled down?
options: They may become insoluble and separate from the solvent
They will dissolve much more quickly
They will spontaneously turn into gas
Their total mass in the mixture will decrease to zero

questions.question: Which of the following sets of factors can affect the solubility of a substance?
options: Only the shape of the beaker used
The size of the solute pieces, the choice of solvent, or the temperature of the solvent
Only the colour of the solute particles
The room's atmospheric pressure and the height of the workbench

questions.question: In a scientific investigation, what is the independent variable?
options: The factor that is kept the same to ensure a fair test
The factor that is observed or measured to see how it responds
The factor that is purposely changed in the investigation
The unit of measurement used to record the final values

questions.question: Why is only one variable changed at a time in a fair test?
options: To make the practical investigation as slow as possible
To make sure that the mass of the reactants increases
So that it is clear that the changed variable made a difference to the results
To prevent any chemical reactions from occurring
